scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Isos Sinasos originates from the town of Sinasos (now Mustafapaşa) in the Cappadocia region of Asia Minor.
Preserved by the Greek community of the region, the dance is executed in a unique local style.
Historical research by Kyriakos Vlasiadis documents its role in regional cultural heritage.
on_screen: Map: Turkey · Middle East
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Isos Sinasos served as a social and communal tradition connecting the village.
The specific gesture of joining three fingers carries religious significance, explicitly representing the Holy Trinity.
The performance environment involved social interaction, where young men shouted comments and taunts to distract the female dancers.
Today it is a historical tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed by women arranged in pairs.
Its footwork mirrors the steps found in the handkerchief and spoon dance of Varasos.
Movement is propelled through rhythmic hand and arm gestures, with dancers joining three fingers together to signify the Holy Trinity.
Watch for Holy Trinity gesture.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Kyriakos Vlasiadis is noted for his ethnomusicological research on the songs and dances from Sinasos, published by ERKET.
The dance represents a style specific to Sinasos in Cappadocia, sharing footwork patterns with the dance of handkerchiefs and spoons from nearby Varasos.
Categorised as a Cappadocian Greek folk dance from Asia Minor, it forms part of the broader family of Anatolian Greek dance traditions.
